key_insight: A small, carefully chosen subset of benchmark datasets can often preserve the global ranking of machine learning models, but the benefit depends strongly on the task domain and dataset representations.
engineering_relevance: This work helps reduce benchmark cost by showing when evaluation can be compressed to a few representative tasks without losing much ranking fidelity, which is useful for faster model selection and benchmarking pipelines.
method: Compared dataset subset selection strategies using bootstrap aggregation to estimate valid confidence intervals for ranking preservation.
Evaluated clustering, A/D-optimal design, random baselines, and greedy farthest-first (FAFI) selection.
Analyzed ranking error bounds for FAFI as a function of the number of selected datasets.
evidence_signal: Across 112 time series datasets and 57 NLP tasks, several strategies beat random subsets; in TSC, five selected datasets achieved Spearman correlation 0.95 with full-benchmark rankings.
watch_item: Selection gains are not universal: on recommender-system benchmarks, improvements over random were small and often not statistically significant, so subset quality should be validated per domain.
paper_title: Benchmarking on Tasks That Matter: Dataset Selection for Preserving Model Rankings
